ticker_lineage_notice: RTO.NZ is the live, currently-quoted continuation of BGI.NZ. The company was renamed from Blackwell Global Holdings Limited to RTO Limited and its NZX ticker changed from BGI to RTO effective 1 May 2024, followed by a 73.6259:1 share consolidation completed 30 August 2024 (673,759,059 shares reduced to 10,000,026 shares). Yahoo/other feeds still carrying a 'BGI.NZ' quote are frozen at a pre-consolidation, pre-rename price and share count and should not be used; RTO.NZ (last close ~NZ$0.118-0.16, mid-Aug 2026) on 10,000,026 shares is the correct instrument.
overview: RTO Limited is a dormant, non-operating cash shell listed on the NZX Main Board with no revenue-generating business. It previously operated a financial-services/mortgage-lending business as Blackwell Global Holdings Limited, discontinued in the year ended 31 March 2023. Since then its sole activity has been searching for a private company to bring public via a reverse takeover (RTO) transaction, which is why it renamed itself RTO Limited in 2024 — the ticker and company name are themselves the investment thesis.

business_model.summary: There is no operating business and no conventional revenue model. The company's only 'product' is its NZX Main Board listing itself, which has scarcity/optionality value to a private company seeking a faster, cheaper route to public markets than a traditional IPO. FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026) total income was $70,031, comprised of $69,000 of 'other income' (a reverse-listing cost reimbursement, likely from a director-related company) plus $1,031 of bank interest on the cash balance — neither is repeatable operating revenue. Costs are the fixed overhead of maintaining a listed shell: directors' fees ($138,000, ~57% of total FY2026 expenses of $243,862), audit, NZX fees, insurance, and share registry costs, producing a $173,831 net loss for the year (versus a $55,236 net loss in FY2025).

revenue_streams.name: Bank interest on shell cash balance
revenue_streams.trend: declining (cash balance shrinking each year: $634,842 at 1-Apr-2024 to $114,903 at 31-Mar-2026)

revenue_streams.name: Reimbursements / other income (non-recurring)
revenue_streams.trend: erratic and non-operating — $300,000 in FY2025, $69,000 in FY2026, driven by one-off reimbursement/related-party items rather than any business

business_model.customer_type: None. No customers, no products, no employees. Sole counterparties are the auditor (William Buck), NZX, the share registry, and the majority shareholder providing funding support.
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand incorporated and NZX-listed (Auckland registered office); majority shareholder Blackwell Global Group Limited is Cayman Islands-incorporated, its controlling individual (Mr Kaw (Michael) Sing Chai) linked to a Singapore-based group.

main_competitors: Other dormant/thinly-traded NZX shells seeking RTO deals
Traditional NZX/ASX IPO process (the alternative route to listing for a target company)
ASX and other exchange shell/backdoor-listing vehicles competing for the same private-company targets
Private equity / trade buyers competing for the same acquisition targets RTO Limited is chasing
competitive_position.market_position: Nano-cap dormant shell; not a market participant in any operating industry. Its only differentiated position is being an already-listed NZX Main Board vehicle with a clean (audited, going-concern-qualified but current) reporting history and a majority shareholder willing to fund overheads.

moat_factors.description: Avoids the time, cost and execution risk of a fresh IPO for a private company wanting to go public via reverse listing; this listing is essentially the company's only asset of note beyond cash.
No debt (secured bonds fully forgiven/converted in Aug 2024); minimal payables, making it a simple, low-friction acquisition vehicle for a target's advisers to work with.

moat_factors.factor: Committed majority shareholder as funding backstop
moat_factors.description: Blackwell Global Group Limited (~74.08% owner) has repeatedly forgiven debt, converted bonds to equity, and committed a further ~$200,000 shareholder loan around July 2026 — reducing near-term insolvency risk but increasing dilution risk and related-party dependence.
No operating brand; the prior mortgage-lending business was wound down in FY2023 and offers no ongoing goodwill.
Not applicable — no operations to scale.

weaknesses: No operating business, no revenue-generating assets, no employees
Extreme illiquidity — average daily trading volume reported around 937 shares, with many sessions in the single digits to low hundreds, making any meaningful position difficult to build or exit
Ongoing operating losses funded entirely by shareholder capital injections and loans, not by any business activity
Heavy concentration risk: Blackwell Global Group Limited ~74.08%, plus ~7.59% held by the same controlling individual (Mr Kaw (Michael) Sing Chai) — over 81% combined control by one interest group
No tangible operating track record to attract acquisition targets other than the listing shell itself
Tax losses of ~$3.9 million carried forward are of uncertain future value given continuity-of-shareholders rules that an RTO transaction (large new share issuance to vendors) would likely breach

growth_drivers: Successful completion of a reverse takeover transaction bringing in an operating business with real earnings — this is the entire investment thesis and the only credible growth driver
Ability to raise additional 'growth capital' alongside any RTO completion, as flagged in the chairman's report as part of the intended process

Continued financial support from majority shareholder Blackwell Global Group Limited, which has both forgiven debt and committed further funding (a ~$200,000 shareholder loan around July 2026), extending the runway during which a deal can be found

NZX's principles-based (rather than prescriptive profit/NTA/working-capital) listing eligibility framework, which does not impose an automatic delisting trigger purely for being non-operating, giving the board more time than a stricter regime might allow

A July-August 2026 shareholder director-nomination process (open 21 Jul-7 Aug 2026) is a normal governance mechanism ahead of the annual meeting; it could refresh the board with directors more suited to executing a transaction, though nothing disclosed publicly ties it to a specific incoming deal

business.description: The company generates no product or service revenue; its entire value proposition depends on management successfully identifying, negotiating and completing an RTO — an outcome that has not occurred despite 'discussions with several potential acquisition targets' as recently as the FY2026 annual report (24 June 2026).

There is no disclosed deadline or committed target; the board has been searching for years (business discontinued FY2023, renamed RTO Limited May 2024) without success. A prospective investor has no visibility on timing or probability of a transaction.

Any acquisition would almost certainly be funded via substantial new share issuance to vendors and/or a capital raise, heavily diluting existing minority holders and potentially changing control. Deal terms (valuation of the incoming asset relative to the shell) would be set by the counterparty and the controlling shareholder, not by minority holders.

financial.description: Cash of $114,903 at 31 March 2026 against an annual cash burn of $173,632 (FY2026 operating outflow) implies well under one year of runway at the current burn rate absent further funding.

The FY2026 audit opinion (William Buck, 24 June 2026) includes an explicit material uncertainty related to going concern, citing the net loss, operating cash outflow, and dependence on identifying a suitable RTO and on ongoing shareholder support.

Going-concern basis rests explicitly on 'ongoing financial support from the majority shareholder,' including a ~$200,000 shareholder loan agreement entered into after the 31 March 2026 balance date and expected to be advanced around July 2026. Withdrawal of this support would leave the shell unable to meet obligations.

Equity fell from $360,956 (31-Mar-2025) to $187,125 (31-Mar-2026), roughly halving in one year, and has swung repeatedly over prior years purely via capital injections/forgiveness and losses, not operations (FY2018 ~$1.53m down to FY2021 ~$0.19m, back up to FY2023 ~$0.41m, down to FY2024 ~$0.17m, up to FY2025 ~$0.36m, down to FY2026 ~$0.19m).

regulatory.description: While NZX does not apply prescriptive profit/working-capital/NTA eligibility criteria the way some exchanges do, a persistently non-operating issuer with a going-concern qualification carries elevated risk of increased NZX scrutiny, potential suspension, or eventual delisting if no transaction materialises and shareholder funding support lapses. No explicit shell-clock deadline was identified in public sources, but this is a standing structural risk for any long-dormant listed shell.

Blackwell Global Group Limited's ~74.08% stake (plus ~7.59% held by the same controlling individual) means any RTO structuring or further share issuance must navigate NZ Takeovers Code constraints; the 2024 bond-to-equity conversion already used the Code's 'creep' provisions, showing the majority holder is willing and able to increase its stake incrementally.

Carried-forward tax losses (unrecognised, historically ~$3.9 million) could shelter future profits of an acquired business, but utilisation depends on continuity-of-shareholders requirements that a reverse takeover — which typically issues large numbers of new shares to vendors — could jeopardise.

macro.description: As a nano-cap shell with negligible free float turnover (average volume ~937 shares/day per third-party data), the stock is highly exposed to general NZX small-cap sentiment and illiquidity discounts/premiums that have little to do with fundamentals.

The attractiveness and pricing of a backdoor listing (versus a traditional IPO or trade sale) for a prospective target depends on broader capital markets conditions; a weak IPO market can make RTO shells more attractive, while a strong one can reduce demand for the shell route.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Not applicable in the traditional sense — RTO Limited has no industry exposure of its own. Its prospects depend entirely on (a) the pool of private NZ/international companies seeking a lower-cost route to public markets via reverse listing, and (b) the board's ability to identify and execute a deal with one of them. Broader NZX Main Board listing volumes and appetite for small-cap new listings are the relevant proxy indicator.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Not operationally cyclical (no business), but the value of the shell option is likely counter-cyclical to IPO market strength: RTOs become relatively more attractive to private companies when traditional IPO markets are weak or expensive.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Minimal direct sensitivity — the company holds modest cash ($114,903 at 31-Mar-2026) earning floating interest, so higher NZ rates marginally help the tiny interest income line but are immaterial to the overall loss.
key_input_costs: Directors' fees ($138,000/yr, ~57% of total FY2026 expenses)
Legal/accounting/consulting costs, which can spike materially around any live RTO negotiation ($224,198 of other operating expenses in FY2025 versus $105,862 in FY2026)

recent_developments.event: NZX 'Call for Director Nominations' announcement released, opening a shareholder nomination window from 21 July 2026 to 5pm 7 August 2026 for shareholders to propose director candidates ahead of the annual meeting. This is a standard governance process; no disclosed link to a specific incoming RTO transaction was found.

FY2026 annual report released: net loss $173,831 (vs $55,236 in FY2025), cash down to $114,903 (from $288,535), equity down to $187,125 (from $360,956). Auditor William Buck issued a material uncertainty related to going concern paragraph. Chairman's report confirms discussions with several potential RTO targets during the year, none yet converted into a tangible transaction, and states the board is 'hopeful of having a transaction underway during the course of this calendar year' (2026).

Company entered into a further ~$200,000 shareholder loan agreement with majority shareholder Blackwell Global Group Limited, after the 31 March 2026 balance date, explicitly relied upon by directors to support the going-concern basis of preparation.
No new shares issued during the year; share count held flat at 10,000,026 for the second consecutive year following the August 2024 consolidation.
Completed a 73.6259:1 share consolidation, reducing shares on issue from 673,759,059 to 10,000,026.

Blackwell Global Group Limited converted $250,000 of secured bonds into new shares (pre-consolidation) using Takeovers Code 'creep' provisions, and forgave the remaining balance of bonds with immediate effect (following an earlier tranche of debt forgiveness in April 2024) — eliminating all debt from the balance sheet.
Company renamed from Blackwell Global Holdings Limited to RTO Limited; NZX ticker changed from BGI to RTO.
Discontinued its previously-operated financial services (mortgage lending) business, becoming non-trading from that point forward.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Sean Joyce reiterated that the company undertook no business activities during FY2026, that the board is actively engaged in seeking an RTO target satisfying criteria such as strong management, a robust business model, solid historical earnings (or a credible plan to generate them), proprietary IP, growth potential (organic, acquisitive, or via capital investment), international scalability, and a need for additional capital that a public listing could satisfy. Management explicitly frames the company itself as 'an attractive vehicle for a reverse takeover transaction.' No specific target, sector focus, or transaction timetable has been disclosed publicly as of this analysis.

bull_case: Pure optionality: any completed RTO with a genuinely viable operating business would represent a step-change in value versus a ~$187,000 net-asset shell, and the market's multi-times premium to NTA shows investors are already pricing some odds of a deal happening
Clean balance sheet with no debt (all bonds forgiven or converted in 2024) makes RTO Limited a simple, low-friction vehicle for a private company's advisers to structure a reverse listing around

Committed, deep-pocketed majority shareholder (Blackwell Global Group Limited, ~74.08%) has repeatedly funded the shell — forgiving bonds, injecting equity, and now committing a further ~$200,000 loan around July 2026 — reducing near-term risk of an uncontrolled insolvency before a deal can be found
Carried-forward tax losses (historically ~$3.9 million) could shelter future profits of an acquired business if shareholder-continuity requirements can be navigated as part of deal structuring

NZX's principles-based listing framework (no strict profit/NTA/working-capital eligibility test) gives the board more runway to find a deal than a stricter exchange regime might allow, and the July-August 2026 director-nomination process shows the governance machinery is still active and open to shareholder input
bear_case: There is no business, no revenue, and no realistic near-term prospect of either absent a completed RTO that has been 'discussed' but not delivered for multiple years running (business discontinued FY2023, renamed to RTO Limited May 2024, still a shell as of the 24 June 2026 annual report and as of this analysis on 13 August 2026)

Going-concern qualified accounts and a cash runway of well under one year at the FY2026 burn rate ($173,632 annual operating outflow against $114,903 cash) mean further dilution or shareholder bailouts are all but certain if no deal completes soon

Extreme illiquidity (average volume reported around 937 shares/day, with many sessions far lower) means the quoted market cap is not achievable in size — a large holder could not exit without materially moving the price, and the last-traded price may not reflect a price at which any real quantity could transact

Market cap trades at a large multiple of net tangible assets (~$187,000 equity versus a market cap of roughly $1.2-1.6 million at prices seen in mid-2026), with the entire premium representing pure speculative optionality on an unspecified, unscheduled, unproven future transaction — if no RTO materialises, the natural anchor for the shares is closer to book value (or lower, given the ongoing burn), implying substantial downside

Over 81% combined control by a single related-party interest group (Blackwell Global Group Limited plus its controlling individual Mr Kaw (Michael) Sing Chai) leaves minority shareholders with limited influence over deal selection, terms, valuation of the incoming asset, or the pace and structure of any dilutive capital raise — minorities are price-takers on any transaction this group agrees to
